item.title: Fármaco de Amgen combinado con inmunoterapia prolonga supervivencia en ensayo clínico sobre cáncer de pulmón
item.description: El fármaco Imdelltra de Amgen, en combinación con Imfinzi de AstraZeneca , redujo el riesgo de muerte en un 58% en comparación con la inmunoterapia de AstraZeneca utilizado en monoterapia en pacientes con cáncer de pulmón microcítico en estadio extenso, según los datos de un estudio presentado el sábado.
item.dc:creator: Deena Beasley
item.content:encoded: El fármaco Imdelltra de Amgen, en combinación con Imfinzi de AstraZeneca (AZN.L) , redujo el riesgo de muerte en un 58% en comparación con la inmunoterapia de AstraZeneca utilizado en monoterapia en pacientes con cáncer de pulmón microcítico en estadio extenso, según los datos de un estudio presentado el sábado. Imfinzi es actualmente el tratamiento de referencia tras la quimioterapia para los pacientes con esta enfermedad tan agresiva y difícil de tratar, cuyo cáncer no empeora tras la quimioterapia inicial. El estudio reveló que los pacientes a los que se administraron ambos fármacos vivieron una mediana de 21,1 meses, frente a los 12,7 meses de los tratados únicamente con Imfinzi. "Si se administra Imdelltra antes, se obtiene un mayor beneficio clínico", afirmó Paul Burton, director médico de Amgen (AMGN.O) , quien calificó los resultados de "sin precedentes en el avance del tratamiento del cáncer de pulmón de células pequeñas en estadio extenso". El fármaco de Amgen está actualmente autorizado para adultos en estadios avanzados de cáncer de pulmón de células pequeñas que ha empeorado a pesar de la quimioterapia, basándose en datos que muestran que Imdelltra redujo el riesgo de muerte en un 40%. Los resultados completos del ensayo, en el que participaron 563 pacientes, se presentaron en el congreso de la Sociedad Europea de Oncología Médica en Madrid y se publicaron en la revista "New England Journal of Medicine". Amgen ya había anunciado anteriormente que el estudio de fase III había tenido éxito. Imdelltra pertenece a una clase de fármacos de doble diana denominados anticuerpos biespecíficos, diseñados para atraer a las células T del sistema inmunitario hacia las células cancerosas con el fin de destruirlas. Imfinzi es un tipo más antiguo de inmunoterapia que, básicamente, bloquea el mecanismo que utilizan los tumores para esconderse del ataque del sistema inmunitario. La mayoría de los casos de cáncer de pulmón son de células no pequeñas, mientras que hasta un 15% corresponde a la variedad de células pequeñas a la que se dirige Imdelltra. Muy pocas personas diagnosticadas con cáncer de pulmón de células pequeñas son candidatas a cirugía, y a la mayoría se les administra inicialmente radioterapia y quimioterapia, explicó Burton. Las tasas de supervivencia dependen del momento en que se diagnostica el cáncer, pero la tasa global a cinco años es solo de alrededor del 9%, según la Sociedad Americana contra el Cáncer. Amgen señaló que, mientras continúa el seguimiento de los pacientes, casi el 80% de los participantes en el ensayo tratados con la combinación seguían vivos al cabo de un año, frente al 53% de los que recibían solo Imfinzi. Se produjeron efectos secundarios graves, entre ellos un recuento bajo de glóbulos blancos, en el 20,9% de los pacientes que recibieron la terapia dual y en el 10,8% de los que recibieron la terapia en monoterapia. Se notificó una afección potencialmente peligrosa conocida como síndrome de liberación de citocinas —una respuesta inflamatoria agresiva— en el 49,6% de los pacientes que recibieron Imdelltra. Sin embargo, solo un caso fue grave y no se produjeron fallecimientos relacionados con ese síndrome.

item.title: Libya's Dbeibah says ready to address Egypt's maritime concerns
item.description: The prime minister of Libya's UN-recognised Government of National Unity told Egypt's intelligence chief his government was ready to address Cairo's concerns over Mediterranean maritime boundaries and economic waters, his office said on Saturday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The prime minister of Libya's UN-recognised Government of National Unity told Egypt's intelligence chief his government was ready to address Cairo's concerns over Mediterranean maritime boundaries and economic waters, his office said on Saturday. Prime Minister Abdulhamid Dbeibah and the intelligence chief Hassan Rashad discussed bilateral relations and coordination on matters of mutual interest during a phone call, the statement said Egypt rejected on Wednesday a maritime boundaries agreement ratified by Libya's eastern-based parliament involving Turkey, saying the deal was null and void and would have no legal effect on Egypt The Libya-Turkey maritime deal was [USN:KBN1Y21VL TEXT:"originally agreed"] in 2019 by Libya's internationally recognised government in Tripoli The rival eastern administration, under military commander Khalifa Haftar, withheld its approval for years The agreement is part of a long-running dispute over maritime claims and energy exploration rights in the eastern Mediterranean Greece, Egypt and Cyprus have opposed the Libya-Turkey accord, saying it infringes their own maritime claims Libya has been divided between Dbeibah's UN-recognised government in Tripoli and eastern authorities aligned with Haftar Egypt and Libya, which share a land border, have longstanding security and economic ties

item.title: Iran has ramped up efforts to target US personnel, intelligence memo warns
item.description: Iran has ramped up efforts to target US personnel, and lethal plots by Tehran against American citizens have reached "advanced stages", a senior intelligence official in the Trump administration warned in a memo seen by Reuters.
item.dc:creator: Humeyra Pamuk, Enas Alashray
item.content:encoded: Iran has ramped up efforts to target US personnel, and lethal plots by Tehran against American citizens have reached "advanced stages", a senior intelligence official in the Trump administration warned in a memo seen by Reuters. The alert from Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton came after Washington scaled back staffing at its mission in Saudi Arabia earlier this week in response to intensified attacks by Iran-allied Houthi forces. Those attacks on one front of the nearly eight-month-old regional conflict triggered by the Iran war have coincided with [USN:L8N4682UH TEXT:"a rise in attacks"] on commercial shipping in the Strait of Hormuz. Earlier this month, sources told Reuters Iran was preparing a [USN:L8N45M1N4 TEXT:"more forceful response"] if the United States resumes large-scale military attacks on its territory. "Specifically, through various channels, we have received intelligence that Iran has substantially increased efforts to target US personnel," Clayton wrote to US Secretary of State Marco Rubio in a message dated October 23. "The lethal plotting efforts by the Iranians against US citizens have reached advanced stages in both the Middle East and certain other countries," he added. CIA Director John Ratcliffe was also copied in on the unclassified memo which was first reported by Axios. The State Department on Wednesday [USN:L6N46718Z TEXT:"ordered"] non-emergency government employees and their family members to leave US diplomatic missions in Saudi Arabia and planned to withdraw family members from a number of other missions in the region, US officials told Reuters. On Saturday, the US State Department updated travel advisories for more than a dozen countries across the Gulf and Middle East, including Saudi Arabia, Qatar, the United Arab Emirates, Iraq and Israel, citing an increased threat from Iran-aligned Houthis. "When it comes to our staffing at embassies, we constantly evaluate new information about the security environment," a US official said. "The threat of Houthi attacks and of Iranian terror plots targeting US officials are informing our decisions on staffing adjustments for embassies on RO Status in the region," the official said. The Restricted Operations Status provides the State Department more flexibility in personnel decisions without having to publicly announce a change in the status of a mission. The Iran war is a week away from entering its ninth month and has significantly weighed on the approval ratings of US President Donald Trump ahead of midterm elections on November 3.

item.title: RB Leipzig thump Elversberg in Bundesliga as Philippe sinks Hamburg
item.description: Romulo Cardoso scored twice for RB Leipzig as they thumped promoted Elversberg 4-0 to climb up to fifth in the Bundesliga on Saturday, while Werder Bremen edged Mainz in a five-goal thriller and Paderborn beat Hamburg.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Romulo Cardoso scored twice for RB Leipzig as they thumped promoted Elversberg 4-0 to climb up to fifth in the Bundesliga on Saturday, while Werder Bremen edged Mainz in a five-goal thriller and Paderborn beat Hamburg. Tidiam Gomis and Christoph Baumgartner, in his first Bundesliga game of the season after injury, were also on target for Leipzig, who have now won all four home games this season but lost all three on road. Elversberg have acquitted themselves well in their maiden top-flight season but were well beaten in Leipzig. Werder Bremen climbed to sixth with a 3-2 victory at Mainz as a pair of Niclas Fullkrug penalties inside the opening 25 minutes gave them the perfect start. Mainz pulled back a goal but Ludovit Reis made it 3-1 and despite the hosts netting again, Bremen were able to hold on for the win. Fullkrug took his tally of goals this season to eight and leads the scorers' charts in the Bundesliga having scored in his last six league matches. Rayan Philippe netted a winning goal two minutes from the end as Paderborn moved out of the bottom three with a 1-0 win at home to Hamburg. Philippe joined Paderborn on loan from Hamburg this season and came off the bench against his parent club, choosing not to celebrate despite the enormity of the goal for his side. There was a goal and a red card each for Augsburg and Union Berlin as they played to a 1-1 draw. Both teams were down to 10 men before the first goal was scored as Felix Uduokhai got his marching orders for Union and Juma Bah was sent off for the home side. Han-Noah Massengo put the hosts ahead on 71 minutes but they had to settle for a point when Janik Haberer equalised for the visitors three minutes later. Cologne and Schalke played to a 0-0 draw as the latter dropped into the bottom three.

item.title: Belgian protesters and police skirmish at anti-government demonstrations in Brussels
item.description: The clashes were smaller than those that took place last week in Belgium and France.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Belgian police used tear gas and pepper spray as they clashed in Brussels on Saturday with anti-government demonstrators calling for better conditions in the education system, Reuters witnesses and Belgian media reported. The clashes came after hundreds of mainly young protesters gathered in a continuation of [USN:L6N46303L TEXT:"rallies"] that have taken place in recent months, calling for more funding for education and accusing police of excessive violence. The clashes were much smaller and less violent than those that took place last week in Belgium and — on a far larger scale — in [USN:L2N46A01A TEXT:"neighbouring France"]. In one incident in Brussels on Saturday, protesters ran and fell to the ground as police pursued them, with officers hitting and kicking one demonstrator, Reuters witnesses saw. Protesters threw road signs and other items onto a pile of rental scooters and bicycles and attempted to set it on fire. In another incident, police used tear gas to disperse a group of protesters, multiple Belgian media outlets reported. Brussels police said in a statement at the end of the afternoon that no major incidents had taken place. They said they had taken measures "to guarantee the maintenance of public order and the security of everyone". Police officers temporarily detained five people for disturbing public order and detained four more for possessing prohibited weapons and for inciting rioting, the statement said.

item.title: Accuser in Cornell rape allegations can stay anonymous, judge rules
item.description: The woman at the center of rape allegations against Cornell University students can keep using a pseudonym in her lawsuit, a judge ruled.
item.dc:creator: Milana Vinn
item.content:encoded: The woman at the center of rape allegations against Cornell University students can keep using a pseudonym in her lawsuit, a judge ruled. New York state Judge Phaedra Perry-Bond ruled on Friday that the accuser's privacy interests, particularly concerns for her safety, outweighed the need to publicly disclose her identity in court proceedings. The woman, who alleges she was drugged and raped by Cornell University students in 2024, has been the [USN:L6N45Q09V TEXT:"target of threats"], her lawyer, Thomas Giuffra, said earlier this month. Although the defendants in the lawsuit did not oppose the request for anonymity, Perry-Bond wrote that "some members of the public have made it their mission to try and identify Jane Doe." The judge warned that "cyberstalking and engaging in or encouraging threats across state lines, whether it be of Jane Doe, of any of the named defendants, or their attorneys, can be considered a federal crime and perpetrators of those acts may be subjecting themselves to prosecution." The woman, who was 20 at the time of the alleged gang rape, filed her suit on September 16, prompting prosecutors to reopen a criminal investigation they had initially closed without charges.

item.title: Report: Indiana RB Khobie Martin to return vs. Michigan
item.description: Indiana running back Khobie Martin is expected to return from a six-game absence and play against Michigan on Saturday afternoon, ESPN reported.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Indiana running back Khobie Martin is expected to return from a six-game absence and play against Michigan on Saturday afternoon, ESPN reported. Martin has been sidelined since sustaining a broken forearm in the Hoosiers' season-opening 52-16 victory over North Texas on Sept. 5. The junior did not record a carry in the game. Martin rushed 78 times for 505 yards (6.5-yard average) and six touchdowns in 14 games as Indiana marched to an undefeated national championship season in 2025. Turbo Richards leads Indiana (6-1, 3-1) this season with a Big Ten-best 643 rushing yards and six touchdowns. Lee Beebe Jr. has 575 yards and four scores on the ground. Michigan (4-2, 1-2) and sixth-ranked Indiana are meeting in Ann Arbor, Mich. --Field Level Media

item.title: Ex-NBA G Malik Beasley negotiating plea in gambling case
item.description: Malik Beasley's attorney says the former NBA guard is working on a plea deal in his federal betting and bribery case.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Malik Beasley's attorney says the former NBA guard is working on a plea deal in his federal betting and bribery case. Attorney Steve Haney told ESPN on Saturday that Beasley, 29, is negotiating with Department of Justice prosecutors and a decision is expected early next week. A recent notice posted on the court docket indicated that he intends to plead guilty, according to ESPN. The U.S. Attorney's Office in the Eastern District of New York alleges that Beasley deliberately manipulated his statistics in at least four games to benefit gamblers while he was playing for the Milwaukee Bucks in 2023-24. Beasley, who played for six teams in nine seasons in the NBA from 2016-25, was indicted on federal charges in June. He initially pleaded not guilty to all counts of bribery in sporting contests, wire fraud conspiracy, honest services wire fraud conspiracy and money laundering conspiracy. The indictment alleges that Beasley lost millions of dollars gambling during his career and agreed to adjust his performance so his alleged co-conspirators could wager on his statistics. Beasley, a first-round pick in the 2016 NBA Draft by Denver, earned nearly $60 million in his NBA career. He averaged 11.7 points in 578 games with the Nuggets, Minnesota Timberwolves, Utah Jazz, Los Angeles Lakers, Bucks and Detroit Pistons. Former NBA player Ed Davis also was charged in the case and has pleaded not guilty. --Field Level Media

item.title: Ataques ucranianos dejan sin electricidad a Crimea y a las zonas controladas por Rusia: Moscú
item.description: Ataques ucranianos provocaron el sábado cortes de electricidad en algunas zonas de Crimea y en las áreas del este y el sur de Ucrania controladas por Rusia, informó el Ministerio de Energía ruso.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Ataques ucranianos provocaron el sábado cortes de electricidad en algunas zonas de Crimea y en las áreas del este y el sur de Ucrania controladas por Rusia, informó el Ministerio de Energía ruso. Los ataques afectaron la infraestructura energética, lo que provocó cortes en algunas zonas de las regiones de Jersón, Zaporiyia, Donetsk y Lugansk, añadió. El ministerio no precisó cuántas personas se habían visto afectadas en esas zonas y en la península de Crimea, que fue anexionada por Rusia en 2014. El personal estaba trabajando para restablecer los servicios y se habían realizado cortes temporales de electricidad para mantener la estabilidad de la red, añadió.

item.title: China insta a EEUU a que frene ampliación propuesta de restricciones a la inversión en el extranjero
item.description: El Ministerio de Comercio chino instó el sábado a Estados Unidos a que dejara de ampliar las restricciones a las inversiones en China, alegando que una norma propuesta sobre tecnologías sensibles perturbaría las relaciones comerciales.
item.dc:creator: Eduardo Baptista
item.content:encoded: El Ministerio de Comercio chino instó el sábado a Estados Unidos a que dejara de ampliar las restricciones a las inversiones en China, alegando que una norma propuesta sobre tecnologías sensibles perturbaría las relaciones comerciales. El Departamento del Tesoro publicó el jueves una serie de propuestas para actualizar su programa de seguridad en materia de inversiones en el extranjero, añadiendo la biotecnología a los sectores restringidos y ampliando el alcance de la normativa a la informática de alto rendimiento y los sistemas hipersónicos. El Ministerio de Comercio de Pekín afirmó en un comunicado que la propuesta amplía "de forma discriminatoria" las restricciones a las inversiones relacionadas con China e intensifica las limitaciones, añadiendo que se opone firmemente a la propuesta estadounidense y se reserva el derecho a adoptar contramedidas que no especificó. Pekín también señaló que la propuesta dañaría las relaciones económicas bilaterales y era contraria al consenso alcanzado por los presidentes de ambos países, que se han reunido en dos ocasiones en los últimos seis meses. El Tesoro ha declarado que las medidas, que no se limitan a China, buscan impedir que el capital estadounidense financie el desarrollo, por parte de adversarios extranjeros, de tecnologías estratégicas de doble uso que podrían amenazar la seguridad nacional. El programa ya había restringido determinadas inversiones estadounidenses relacionadas con China en los ámbitos de los semiconductores, las tecnologías cuánticas y la inteligencia artificial.

item.title: Trump afirma que podría trasladar a la prensa acreditada en la Casa Blanca
item.description: El presidente Donald Trump confirmó el sábado que podría trasladar a la prensa acreditada en la Casa Blanca a otra ubicación.
item.dc:creator: Jason Lange
item.content:encoded: El presidente Donald Trump confirmó el sábado que podría trasladar a la prensa acreditada en la Casa Blanca a otra ubicación. En una publicación en las redes sociales, Trump desmintió un reporte que señalaba que tenía previsto eliminar la sala de prensa de la Casa Blanca y restaurar una piscina histórica en ese mismo lugar, afirmando que nunca se le había "pasado por la cabeza hacer algo tan estúpido". Sin embargo, señaló que podría reubicar al cuerpo de prensa de su ubicación actual en la Casa Blanca. "Quizá traslade a los de las noticias falsas a un lugar menos molesto", afirmó Trump. El New York Times informó el martes que Trump había instado en agosto a la entonces secretaria de prensa Karoline Leavitt a trasladar las ruedas de prensa fuera de la sala de prensa James S. Brady de la Casa Blanca, aunque la idea nunca se llevó a cabo. Según el reporte, el presidente dijo a sus asesores que preferiría disponer de una piscina terapéutica cubierta que se instaló en ese lugar durante la administración de Franklin D. Roosevelt. El Gobierno de Richard Nixon sustituyó la piscina por la sala de prensa. Trump ha acusado con frecuencia a la prensa estadounidenses de informar de forma sesgada sobre su Gobierno. Trump prohibió temporalmente el mes pasado el acceso a los terrenos de la Casa Blanca a periodistas de CNN, MS NOW y Politico, y afirmó que otros medios podrían enfrentarse a restricciones similares. La Casa Blanca restableció su acceso tras una orden de un juez federal que consideró que la medida era probablemente inconstitucional, aunque el Gobierno sigue impugnando el caso.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro y Lula están prácticamente empatados de cara a balotaje Brasil: encuesta de CNT/MDA
item.description: El senador brasileño Flávio Bolsonaro y el presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva siguen prácticamente empatados de cara a la segunda vuelta electoral del domingo, reveló el sábado una encuesta de CNT/MDA.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: El senador brasileño Flávio Bolsonaro y el presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva siguen prácticamente empatados de cara a la segunda vuelta electoral del domingo, reveló el sábado una encuesta de CNT/MDA. El senador de derecha, hijo mayor del expresidente Jair Bolsonaro, obtendría el 46,3% de los votos, frente al 45% de Lula, según la encuesta. La semana pasada, otro sondeo mostraba a Bolsonaro por delante de Lula con un 46,8% frente a un 45,9%. MDA encuestó a 2.032 personas entre el 21 y el 23 de octubre. El margen de error es de +/-2,2 puntos porcentuales.

item.title: After 'everything went wrong,' Suns eager to make right vs. Warriors
item.description: The Suns and Golden State Warriors -- two teams in various stages of recovery -- will meet in Phoenix on Saturday, when one will break into the win column.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: The Suns and Golden State Warriors -- two teams in various stages of recovery -- will meet in Phoenix on Saturday, when one will break into the win column. The Warriors collapsed late in a 111-108 loss to Memphis in their home opener Friday, giving up 17 straight points after De'Anthony Melton's 3-pointer gave them a 106-94 edge with 3:47 left. "Everything went wrong," guard Stephen Curry said after the Warriors fell to 0-2 for the first time since 2020-21. The Suns hit a similar roadblock in Portland on Wednesday, when they gave up the first 21 points in a 124-83 loss in the Trail Blazers' home opener. "We just absolutely got blitzed," Suns coach Jordan Ott said. Curry scored 24 points against the Grizzlies after finishing with 23 in a 127-105 loss at the Los Angeles Lakers on Wednesday. But he has yet to find his range, going 12-of-30 from the field and 5-of-17 from 3-point range. Before the Memphis game, Warriors coach Steve Kerr outlined a new substitution pattern for Curry as the team seeks to offset the loss of scoring big man Kristaps Porzingis (undisclosed health issue) for the foreseeable future. "He'll play the first seven or eight minutes in the first quarter and then come back at the top of the second for a shorter shift," Kerr said of Curry. "That's how we are starting this year, and we'll see how it goes. It's always flexible." Curry played the first seven minutes of the first quarter Friday and played another seven, including the first 3 1/2 in the second quarter. He had 14 of his points in 15 second-half minutes. The Suns, who eliminated the Warriors in the play-in round 111-96 on April 17, found no rhythm on either side of the ball in Portland. They trailed by as many as 52 points in that game. They shot 35.7% from the field and were outrebounded 56-39. The Trail Blazers made 19 of 47 3-pointers and were in the penalty before the Suns made a field goal. Devin Booker scored 23 points on 7-of-13 shooting, but Dillon Brooks, Jalen Green and newcomer Miles Bridges were a combined 11-of-34 from the floor. The Blazers led 43-12 after the first quarter. "Everything went wrong," Booker said, echoing Curry. "We have a lot to learn from on tape. They were killing us with their pace. It's an uphill battle when you are down 30 points. You feel like every shot has to go in. We just have to get off to a better start." Suns second-year center Khaman Maluach started Wednesday, although both Maluach and third-year player Oso Ighodaro likely are to share post minutes while Mark Williams (left shoulder) is out. Maluach had two points and six rebounds in 17 minutes. "Throwing young guys into the fire ... that's what you see, and he'll learn from this," Ott said. "We need him. We need him to grow. He will continue to grow. We need him to take a step. He'll take steps." Ighodaro left the Portland game in the first half with an apparent right hip injury and did not return. Off guard Luke Kennard (left knee) did not play against the Blazers. The status of each player for Saturday's game is unknown. Warriors guard Brandin Podziemski and rookie Yaxel Lendeborg had 18 points against Memphis. Backup big man Charles Bassey (knee) missed his second straight game. --Field Level Media

item.title: Na véspera do 2º turno, Lula diz que povo assumiu responsabilidade por campanha
item.description: O presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) disse neste sábado que o povo assumiu a responsabilidade por sua campanha no segundo turno da eleição presidencial, marcado para o domingo, e mostrou convicção de que conquistará um quarto mandato presidencial quando a apuração dos votos for realizada.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: O presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) disse neste sábado que o povo assumiu a responsabilidade por sua campanha no segundo turno da eleição presidencial, marcado para o domingo, e mostrou convicção de que conquistará um quarto mandato presidencial quando a apuração dos votos for realizada. Em declaração à imprensa antes de participar de evento de campanha em Copacabana, acompanhado por uma multidão, Lula também fez críticas ao senador Flávio Bolsonaro (PL), seu adversário, que terminou à frente no primeiro turno, realizado no dia 4 de outubro. "Estou dizendo para vocês e podem anotar, amanhã eu serei eleito presidente da República outra vez", afirmou Lula aos jornalistas. "O povo assumiu para si a responsabilidade de fazer a campanha. Hoje nós temos um exército de democratas neste país maior que o Exército chinês, maior que o Exército russo e maior que o Exército americano que é o Exército do Lula, que vai chegar a 13 milhões de soldados e soldadas amanhã", continuou. "E vamos ganhar as eleições por uma simples razão: é verdade que o povo quer mudança, e o povo quer mudança para melhor, o povo quer mudança para frente. O povo não quer retroceder e não está longe da nossa memória o que aconteceu no mandato dessa gente nesse país", acrescentou. Lula se referia ao canal de WhatsApp Exército do Lula, criado pelo deputado federal reeleito André Janones (Rede-MG), no qual o parlamentar passa a apoiadores "missões" para colocar Lula em destaque nas redes sociais e para fazer críticas a Flávio. A fala de Lula sobre a participação popular no segundo turno da campanha vem depois de uma série de críticas à campanha petista no primeiro turno, de dentro e de fora do PT e inclusive do próprio Lula, que em reunião logo após a primeira rodada disse que a campanha até o dia 4 de outubro foi a [USN:L6N45T151 TEXT:""menos organizada""] de que participou desde 1989. Após a passeata em Copacabana, Lula fará à tarde evento de campanha na Avenida Paulista, em São Paulo. No domingo, a previsão é que vote logo cedo pela manhã em São Bernardo do Campo e acompanhe a apuração na capital paulista. Flávio venceu o primeiro turno com 47,03% dos votos válidos contra 45,16% de Lula. As pesquisas de intenção de voto têm mostrado empate técnico entre ambos, com vantagem numérica para o senador. Levantamento [USN:S0N46101Q TEXT:"CNT/MDA"] divulgado neste sábado mostrou Flávio com 46,3% dos votos totais contra 45% de Lula. Nos votos válidos, quando são excluídos brancos, nulos e indecisos, o senador tem 50,7% e o presidente soma 49,3%.

item.title: WTA roundup: No. 1 Elena Rybakina chasing 4th title of '26
item.description: World No. 1 Elena Rybakina will play for her fourth title of the season Sunday at the Ningbo Open in China, opposing Canada's Leylah Fernandez.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: World No. 1 Elena Rybakina will play for her fourth title of the season Sunday at the Ningbo Open in China, opposing Canada's Leylah Fernandez. Both players posted 6-3, 7-5 victories on Saturday. Top-seeded Rybakina, from Kazakhstan, beat No. 6 Diana Shnaider of Russia and Fernandez topped Czech Marie Bouzkova. Rybakina, who won the WTA 500 tournament last year, is seeking the first successful title defense of her career and her 15th career title. Fernandez has six career titles, winning in Singapore in September. Rybakina holds a 3-2 lead in their head-to-head series. Japan Open Ashlyn Krueger defeated fellow American and No. 1 seed Ann Li 6-4, 6-7 (4), 6-3 to earn a place in the finals in Osaka. Li lost serve in the first game of the third set and could not catch up. Serving down 5-3 in the third, Li went up 40-0 and squandered the lead, with Krueger winning on her second match point. Krueger won the title in Osaka in 2023 and is 10-2 in her career at the WTA 250 tournament. She will face Czech Katerina Siniakova, who defeated No. 8 Katie Boulter of Great Britain 6-1, 6-4 in the other semifinal. --Field Level Media
